subject.title: iOS: keychain save fails on fresh install (cal save failed / disconnected because it could not securely save)

question: Should the iOS team require production-signed device diagnostics identifying the exact Keychain OSStatus before authorizing changes to the shared credential-store contract?
rationale: The observable blocker is clear, but the same symptom can result from application logic, entitlements, signing, access groups, or device security state; choosing a repair without that distinction could alter credential handling incorrectly.

options.title: Diagnose signed build first
options.body: Capture redacted device logs and the exact OSStatus on a production-signed fresh install, then make the narrowest evidence-backed Keychain and onboarding repair.

options.title: Add diagnostics immediately
options.body: First change the shared store to return typed Security.framework errors, then use a follow-up signed build to identify and repair the underlying failure.

options.title: Treat as release configuration
options.body: Audit signing, entitlements, and Keychain access groups before changing runtime code, closing only if production configuration fully explains the failure.

recommendation.title: Diagnose signed build first
recommendation.body: Capture redacted device logs and the exact OSStatus on a production-signed fresh install, then make the narrowest evidence-backed Keychain and onboarding repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available feature-history signal is recent work on the iOS companion app's adjacent device-auth and APNs paths.
